module.title: Python -> TypeScript Bridge
module.subtitle: Mapping Python dicts, lists, None, and functions to TypeScript interfaces & types
lesson_points: TypeScript looks like JavaScript with explicit type contracts checked before the code ever runs.
A Python dict schema becomes a TypeScript 'interface' or 'type' describing exact allowed keys.
Python's 'None' splits into 'null' or 'undefined', and TypeScript forces you to check for it with 'if (val !== null)'.

rosetta_pairs.target_code:
let fuel: number = 50;
const name: string = "Valkyrie";
rosetta_pairs.note: TypeScript uses 'let' (reassignable) or 'const' (fixed binding) plus ': type' hints.

rosetta_pairs.target_code:
interface Ship { name: string; fuel: number; }
const ship: Ship = { name: "Nova", fuel: 50 };
rosetta_pairs.note: An interface locks in field names and types so typos fail at compile time instead of runtime.
Union types like 'Ship | null' force you to handle the missing case explicitly.

quizzes.title: Python Equivalent Output
quizzes.prompt: Just like the TypeScript 'ship: Ship | null' helper, what does format_ship(None) print?
quizzes.explanation: The guard 'if ship is None:' returns 'Offline' safely before touching ship['name'].

quizzes.title: Spot the Missing Null Guard
quizzes.prompt: Click the line that crashes if 'ship' is None (the exact bug TypeScript union types prevent!).
quizzes.explanation: Line 2 accesses ship['fuel'] BEFORE checking 'if ship is None:' on line 3.

quizzes.title: Why Use Interfaces?
quizzes.prompt: Why does TypeScript ask you to declare 'interface Ship { name: string; fuel: number }' upfront?
quizzes.code: interface Ship { name: string; fuel: number; }
quizzes.sample_explanation: Interfaces define the exact field names and types upfront so typos or wrong types are caught at compile time before the app runs.
quizzes.explanation: Compile-time structural contracts catch misspelled keys and wrong types immediately.
